hashConvention: SHA-256 of UTF-8 LF sources and exact Pester It AST extent. Parameterized selectors are reviewed as groups.

selectors.selector: reports both CPU slices with explicit no-device selection
selectors.reviewScope: Verifies exact no-device arguments and an unchanged ambient precision at native launch, with an opaque JSON payload delivered to a profile-free shell.

selectors.selector: qualifies <Route> only when reported offload is complete
selectors.reviewScope: Verifies the requested child precision, unchanged parent precision and explicit device arguments during both discovery and timing, with complete observed offload.

selectors.selector: rejects q4 before timing with a <Case> CUDA capability
blocks either wrong digest and incompatible CUDA precision
selectors.reviewScope: Checks both digest mismatches and refusal to apply CUDA precision on Intel before either native call.
Checks absent and ambiguous Intel candidates independently, including the reported number of qualifying devices.

selectors.selector: rejects a success status with no benchmark rows
selectors.reviewScope: Checks that a successful process exit cannot stand in for the expected benchmark rows.

selectors.selector: preserves literal argv, raw streams and exit code with child-only precision
selectors.reviewScope: The production launcher and owned Windows process runner pass literal argv, EOF, separate UTF-8 stdout and stderr, and exit status through an inert workload. The child sees q4, q8 or absence while the parent remains unchanged.

selectors.selector: terminates the native workload at the launcher deadline
selectors.reviewScope: An inert workload records its PID and blocks. The owned job reports timeout, closes the nested workload, and leaves ambient precision unchanged.
